definition: Creates recoverable copies of digital data, on site, off site or in the cloud. Routine storage without a recovery function is insufficient.
Replicates data or systems and enables services to switch to another environment after failure. Do not infer failover from replication alone.
Establishes or uses a secondary computing environment to restore services after disruption. Replication or failover may also qualify when explicit.
Defines technical recovery objectives, plans or tested procedures for digital systems. Generic organisational continuity plans without a technical mechanism are insufficient.
Digitises and backs up physical records explicitly to preserve them against disaster loss. Digitisation alone is insufficient.
